layers.title: Market data and reference
layers.requirement: Acquire licensed, source-identifiable US-equity observations; preserve feed, timestamps, identity and corporate actions; produce exact reproducible analytical snapshots and reject data whose historical availability or eligibility is unknown.
layers.current_choice: Official alpaca-py for the bounded selected market-data path; EdgarTools for selected filing parsing/acquisition; DuckDB and Parquet for local analysis; exchange_calendars for explicit session semantics. Dataset manifests and schema checks are requirements, while DVC/Pandera remain source-reviewed implementation candidates.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row data-research (2026-09-22): Native acquisition, parsing and analytical receipts support these concrete interfaces without a new lake, broker or distributed database. They do not close the actual research bottleneck: a complete point-in-time eligible universe with trustworthy availability, identity and corporate-action semantics. Source-review defaults for DVC/Pandera must not be mistaken for installed acceptance. Databento/Massive are credible conditional alternatives when required coverage or rights cannot be obtained through the selected path.
limitations: The authenticated Alpaca receipt covers 25 AAPL SIP/raw daily bars and two corporate actions over five successful pages, not a survivorship-free universe, complete history or real-time feed entitlement.

Numeric corporate-action values matched the frozen probe, but missing dividend currency prevented full cash-unit reconciliation. Original historical availability and complete action coverage remain open.
Three documentary lifecycle cases preserve observed cutoffs and source anchors; retrospective claims do not establish historical as-known eligibility or permanent security identity.
The prior SEC HTTP 403 remains a historical failure. Later corrected acquisition and parsing qualify their selected requests only; no general filing-completeness or strategy-validity claim follows.
SQL, schemas and content hashes cannot repair missing provenance, revised fundamentals, access rights or outcome-selected samples.
layers.overturn_when: Freeze required universe/history/latency, rights, correction and availability semantics; compare selected providers on representative securities including delistings, ticker reuse and corporate actions, then change the feed/store only when a candidate closes those gaps with auditable records and acceptable measured cost. layers.verdict_overturn_when:
Change the verdict for the prices/corporate-actions scope, replacing c9 with c14 Databento or c7 Massive, when all of the following hold on the frozen sample in blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/plan.json (AAPL, sip/raw 1Day, [2020-08-03, 2020-09-05)):
(a) The challenger arm is scored by a generalized version of blueprints/us-equities/authenticated-data/compare.py. The current script is hard-coded to the Alpaca collector and to AAPL with 25 reference sessions (lines 15-20 and 45-48), so it needs extending first, with its test module tests/test_historical_comparison.py extended alongside it.
(b) The scored arm gives bars 25/25 equal.
(c) The scored arm gives actions status "equal" (2 of 2, including USD currency), where Alpaca left 1 unknown_currency.
(d) Each record carries an auditable historical availability timestamp.
A universe-level overturn, meaning delistings and ticker reuse, first needs a new frozen universe plan, which plan.json's continuation defers.

Regression guards for the custom code the winners rely on are `python3 -m unittest tests.test_historical_comparison tests.test_catalyst_provenance tests.test_alpaca_historical`. The alpaca-py cases need the SDK interpreter: tests/test_alpaca_historical.py:233/237/296/314 call skipTest when the SDK is not installed. A failure invalidates the comparator or adapter logic behind c9's reconciliation and c6's availability gate, not EdgarTools or alpaca-py themselves. These tests run on synthetic/temporary inputs and do not re-validate the retained receipts.

layers.title: Data quality and orchestration
layers.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row agents-operations (2026-09-22): The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under data-research (2); agents-operations (7) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

layers.rationale: Derived from domain row engines-strategies (2026-09-22): The current choice follows the explicit runtime target and supported native IBKR direction, with real installation/replay and bounded AAPL accounting evidence. LEAN has deeper retained SPY stress/dividend/cash evidence and is kept as the comparison oracle rather than relabeled a losing engine. limitations: Nautilus 2.0.0rc5 is a prerelease. The old September 19 Nautilus alternative and LEAN default cards remain historical; runtime-target.json governs the current destination.

The retained AAPL replay has 15 bars and five roundtrips per baseline/stress scenario with reconciled cash; it excludes known action dates and uses retrospective synthetic close fills with unlimited modeled depth.
SPY/LEAN dividend/cash parity is still planned. LEAN's known-crash fixtures are engineering stresses, not untouched holdout results or calibrated broker execution.

The Alpaca trial observed two actual writes, a -0.08 USD cash-matched gross result, flat/idle reconciliation and completed-trial recovery with zero additional writes. In-flight native failure cases, IBKR, live operation and continuous paper operation remain open.
No accepted point-in-time universe, extreme-mover/catalyst strategy, financing-inclusive performance or deployable profitability follows from these receipts.

layers.verdict_overturn_when:
Rerun the bound comparator against the pinned oracle with this command: `python3 blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/spy-parity/compare.py --receipt blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/spy-parity/receipt.json --lean-data <LEAN 985ef30 Data root> --verdict <out>`. The comparator is bound by blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/spy-parity/mapping-manifest.json and tolerances.json.

The verdict changes in any of three cases:
(a) The Nautilus replay returns FAIL, has an unattributed failure or unexplained cash residue, or breaches a preregistered tolerances.json limit.
(b) Nautilus cannot close market_on_open_proxy or distributions_and_cash, either natively or through a newly preregistered mapping manifest, while a maintained alternative engine reaches PASS on the same frozen one_zero inputs, tolerances and hash bindings.
(c) The oracle's own receipt changes. compare.py lines 202-203 raise oracle_receipt_sha256_mismatch when blueprints/us-equities/historical-simulation/receipt.json no longer hashes to 06ec065647abd91a0ca2b13da25dd75c3ccd159a3244a241a3207c58b36f95d9, or when a native LEAN 985ef30 rerun of its one_zero case no longer reproduces fills at 323.58 and 291.69, dividends of 428.64 and end cash of 90734.080. Either would invalidate LEAN's oracle role.

The bundled-sample order_list_hash f209ed42701b0419858e0100595b40c0 in blueprints/us-equities/engine/receipt.json only shows the build is healthy. A regression in it would prompt a rebuild check, not an oracle overturn by itself. In every case the synthetic boundary checks in `python3 -m unittest tests.test_spy_parity -v` must keep passing.

Nautilus native IBKR awaits broker acceptance; Alpaca uses official alpaca-py and a separately qualified deterministic paper path. No strategy is promoted as profitable.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row engines-strategies (2026-09-22): The current choice follows the explicit runtime target and supported native IBKR direction, with real installation/replay and bounded AAPL accounting evidence. LEAN has deeper retained SPY stress/dividend/cash evidence and is kept as the comparison oracle rather than relabeled a losing engine. The AAPL diagnostic and one Alpaca paper roundtrip do not prove SPY parity, realistic liquidity, IBKR operation, continuous paper service or a winning strategy. Existing research modules remain task-specific.
limitations: Nautilus 2.0.0rc5 is a prerelease. The old September 19 Nautilus alternative and LEAN default cards remain historical; runtime-target.json governs the current destination.

The retained AAPL replay has 15 bars and five roundtrips per baseline/stress scenario with reconciled cash; it excludes known action dates and uses retrospective synthetic close fills with unlimited modeled depth.
SPY/LEAN dividend/cash parity is still planned. LEAN's known-crash fixtures are engineering stresses, not untouched holdout results or calibrated broker execution.

The Alpaca trial observed two actual writes, a -0.08 USD cash-matched gross result, flat/idle reconciliation and completed-trial recovery with zero additional writes. In-flight native failure cases, IBKR, live operation and continuous paper operation remain open.
No accepted point-in-time universe, extreme-mover/catalyst strategy, financing-inclusive performance or deployable profitability follows from these receipts.

Independent source review found two bare matches! expressions that do not assert denial-event variants in Nautilus risk tests, also present in v2.0.0rc5 source. Other tests assert denial and reasons. This narrow test defect is not an observed runtime failure; see docs/blind-catalog-source-adjudication-20260921.md.
layers.overturn_when: Reopen the implementation choice if Nautilus cannot preserve a required cash/order semantic, fails a preregistered SPY/LEAN parity tolerance, or a broker-specific adapter cannot pass ownership, reconciliation, partial/cancel/reconnect and numeric risk cases. Compare alternatives on the same frozen inputs and failure contract; promote a strategy only after independent temporal and cost-aware evaluation.

layers.title: Evaluation and experiments
layers.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row agents-operations (2026-09-22): The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under data-research (3), foundation-memory (3); agents-operations (6) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

candidates.rationale: Scoped installation, service and plaintext restore worked, while the September 20 inference attempt hit quota/429 limits and compression previews lost a required value. Keep optional explicit routing with compression disabled; these observations do not prove the gateway universally unusable.

candidates.rationale: The retained Windows-to-WSL health result proves transport only; Claude-like aliases can select local Qwen and do not establish Anthropic identity or Astra inference. It cannot silently replace the native worker.

candidates.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
candidates.rationale: Appropriate for an application-owned API agent with programmatic control when that is the requirement. It has not demonstrated a missing capability in the selected native Codex research path.

candidates.name: vLLM
candidates.rationale: Retain the accepted 0.25.0 WSL embedding runtime: 0.29.0 installed and its CLI ran, but GPU startup failed with unavailable UVA on this host. This is a concrete version/hardware boundary, not a failure of all newer releases or other hosts.

candidates.name: Deep Agents
candidates.rationale: The reviewed harness combines planning, delegated context, filesystem backends and LangGraph persistence. It is a credible prebuilt application-owned worker alternative, including local model routes; neither its README nor the available upstream tests establish better catalog-review accuracy, native-account compatibility or total cost on our tasks.

candidates.name: OpenHands SDK
candidates.rationale: The maintained SDK/Agent Server owns agents, tools, conversations, events and local or ephemeral workspaces; it is a credible isolated/remote-worker implementation. No matched native research, interruption/recovery or complete operating-cost comparison has displaced the accepted worker path.

candidates.name: OpenHands Agent Canvas
candidates.rationale: The current repository is Agent Canvas, a control center able to host OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex and other ACP agents across backends. Treat it as a prospective host for existing native workers, not merely a competing coding model. Its hosting, account boundaries, persistence and migration remain unqualified here.

candidates.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
candidates.rationale: The primary source provides .NET/Python agent applications, provider integrations and graph workflows with checkpoints and handoffs. It closes a source-review coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime gap; qualify a required application workflow and deployment before adoption.

alternatives.name: data-river
alternatives.why_not_default: River's progressive validation is an online-learning tool. It applies only if streaming model updates are justified. The card's own limitations say immediate synthetic labels are invalid for financial online evaluation, and that delayed fills or returns, late corrections and restarts must be modelled. The workflow is marked UNEXECUTED and the evidence is source review only (catalogs/us-equities/data-research.json lines 1304-1340).

alternatives.name: foundation-mteb
alternatives.why_not_default: MTEB evaluates embeddings, which overlaps the executed retrieval evaluation in c7. Its pin (2.21.0) is behind upstream (2.21.6). The card says its commands were not executed (catalogs/us-equities/foundation-memory.json lines 1210-1245). Other retained artifacts mention MTEB: leaderboard Space metadata and author-reported aggregates in evidence/artifacts/hf-memory-models-20260921/model-manifest.json, and leaderboard page observations in evidence/artifacts/hf-memory-models-20260921/dashboard-observations.json lines 15-33. None of them is a run of the mteb library. native-results.json line 475 states "No full RTEB/MTEB rerun".

alternatives.name: phoenix
alternatives.why_not_default: Phoenix is mainly a trace inspection workspace and overlaps the observability layer. The server launch is prospective, with no app instrumented and no judge-model calls run. The card says PHOENIX_ALLOWED_PROVIDERS=NONE is not an inference authorization boundary (catalogs/us-equities/agents-operations.json lines 1239-1280). The card licenses it as Elastic-2.0 (ELv2), which carries self-host restrictions. The packet's NOASSERTION value is GitHub's license classification, not a conflicting license (screening-ledger.json lines 6714 and 10770).

layers.title: Agents, models and workers
layers.requirement: Keep durable project knowledge, exact code and dated financial sources retrievable across native clients, with source recovery, explicit project scope and measurable retrieval quality.
layers.current_choice: ai-memory as the shared memory of record; QMD BM25 for documents; Serena for exact symbols; SocratiCode with Qdrant for conceptual code search; Context Mode and RTK for selected large outputs. These are complementary lanes, not one benchmark winner.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row foundation-memory (2026-09-22): The selected lanes have native operation and recovery evidence on the existing host and avoid making every lookup depend on another extraction model or service. The measured QMD domain fixture returned the intended source in the first three results for 8 of 12 queries, so its low setup cost supports retention while the four misses require a representative comparison before claiming retrieval superiority. Memory recall and code search receipts do not qualify financial answer truth or historical market availability.
limitations: Twelve curated queries are a bounded diagnostic, not an independent holdout or a complete financial RAG evaluation. Exact-source recall at three was 8/12; misses remain recorded.

The eight native answer invocations form four within-provider task comparisons; two Claude full-context answers missed the word protocol and one focused Codex answer scored 9.5 versus 10. These are not general or causal savings results.
Same-host encrypted restore preserved application state, but independent key recovery, off-host durability and new-host client rebinding remain unqualified.
Alternative memory and RAG repositories below were generally source-reviewed, not run head-to-head. A source-only candidate has not failed.

Current primary-source review corrects manual-only, Claude-only and cloud-only exclusions. No matched memory benchmark or new installation was run; automatic capture, local providers and published scores remain source claims until exercised on the selected profile.
The us-equities catalog also tags entries for this taxonomy layer under agents-operations (10); foundation-memory (28) was picked as the primary group by entry count.
layers.overturn_when: Run a preregistered, representative held-out financial/document and code retrieval set at the same context budget; replace or supplement a lane only if a candidate improves source/answer fidelity, abstention and measured task cost while preserving isolation, exact source recovery and native client behavior.

layers.title: Observability and hosting
layers.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
layers.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
layers.rationale: Derived from domain row agents-operations (2026-09-22): The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
layers.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

candidates.rationale: Native independent review and research tasks have returned results and scoped usage observations. Retain this lane while checking actual account readiness and preserving failed or protocol-incomplete attempts.

candidates.name: Dagu
candidates.rationale: The native local scheduler runs existing bounded commands, retains authenticated history and has accepted research packet/Parquet preparation. The historical card's conditional label does not negate those later selected local operations.

candidates.rationale: One accepted distribution supplies privacy transforms and native metric/log delivery. The core Collector repository is a source dependency, not a second collector to install.

candidates.name: Prometheus

candidates.name: Loki
candidates.rationale: The existing privacy-filtered log lane complements metrics and has native process correlation evidence. It does not imply retention of full conversation transcripts.

candidates.name: Grafana
candidates.rationale: It reads the existing Prometheus/Loki stores and has retained dashboard evidence. A new trace/evaluation suite is conditional on a question the current observation stack cannot answer.

candidates.name: Restic
candidates.rationale: Native encrypted backup/restore plus original-application restoration now covers scoped ai-memory and Qdrant state. This supports current local recovery while leaving independent keys and off-host durability open.

candidates.name: Temporal
candidates.rationale: Durable activities, waiting and host-loss recovery are a plausible escalation for multi-day effects. The existing bounded command workload has not demonstrated the need or qualified a Temporal deployment.

candidates.name: Prefect
candidates.rationale: A Python-first flow service can fit scheduling/retries if that becomes the main operational requirement. It remains an alternative to adding another retry owner around current native workflows.

candidates.name: Dagster
candidates.rationale: Partitioned assets, lineage and backfills may justify adoption for the data program. Those merits do not establish benefit for simply dispatching a few native research workers.

candidates.name: LangGraph
candidates.rationale: Explicit agent state/checkpoints can help once branching and resume exceed a bounded native task. No matched task establishes that another agent loop is currently needed.

candidates.name: DeerFlow
candidates.rationale: One retained embedded DeerFlow ACP research prompt completed; current source also documents embedded Python, terminal, sandbox and Claude/native-provider integrations. These are substantial prebuilt capabilities, but the full planner/UI service and current revision have not been locally qualified. The tested adapter's read-only label mapped to workspaceWrite/on-request, so preserve that historical restriction finding rather than assuming the outer harness fixes it.

candidates.name: OmniRoute
candidates.rationale: Scoped installation, service and plaintext restore worked, while the September 20 inference attempt hit quota/429 limits and compression previews lost a required value. Keep optional explicit routing with compression disabled; these observations do not prove the gateway universally unusable.

candidates.name: FreeLLMAPI
candidates.rationale: The retained Windows-to-WSL health result proves transport only; Claude-like aliases can select local Qwen and do not establish Anthropic identity or Astra inference. It cannot silently replace the native worker.

candidates.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
candidates.rationale: Appropriate for an application-owned API agent with programmatic control when that is the requirement. It has not demonstrated a missing capability in the selected native Codex research path.

candidates.name: vLLM
candidates.rationale: Retain the accepted 0.25.0 WSL embedding runtime: 0.29.0 installed and its CLI ran, but GPU startup failed with unavailable UVA on this host. This is a concrete version/hardware boundary, not a failure of all newer releases or other hosts.

candidates.name: Deep Agents
candidates.rationale: The reviewed harness combines planning, delegated context, filesystem backends and LangGraph persistence. candidates.name: OpenHands SDK
candidates.rationale: The maintained SDK/Agent Server owns agents, tools, conversations, events and local or ephemeral workspaces; it is a credible isolated/remote-worker implementation. No matched native research, interruption/recovery or complete operating-cost comparison has displaced the accepted worker path.

candidates.name: OpenHands Agent Canvas
candidates.rationale: The current repository is Agent Canvas, a control center able to host OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex and other ACP agents across backends. Treat it as a prospective host for existing native workers, not merely a competing coding model. Its hosting, account boundaries, persistence and migration remain unqualified here.

candidates.rationale: The primary source provides .NET/Python agent applications, provider integrations and graph workflows with checkpoints and handoffs. It closes a source-review coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime gap; qualify a required application workflow and deployment before adoption.

2. A re-scan with a later Grype database or dependency set records matches with a needs_review disposition.
3. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_gitleaks_config` shows the gitleaks config missing synthetic secret fixtures.
4. A new receipt records a native cosign verification of the Syft/Grype release artifacts (signature_verified true, exact identity), or a native OpenBao secret-lifecycle run. Such a receipt would add cosign or OpenBao to the winner set or replace a winner.

domain_rows.title: Scoped memory and research retrieval
domain_rows.requirement: Keep durable project knowledge, exact code and dated financial sources retrievable across native clients, with source recovery, explicit project scope and measurable retrieval quality.
domain_rows.current_choice: ai-memory as the shared memory of record; QMD BM25 for documents; Serena for exact symbols; SocratiCode with Qdrant for conceptual code search; Context Mode and RTK for selected large outputs. These are complementary lanes, not one benchmark winner.
domain_rows.rationale: The selected lanes have native operation and recovery evidence on the existing host and avoid making every lookup depend on another extraction model or service. The measured QMD domain fixture returned the intended source in the first three results for 8 of 12 queries, so its low setup cost supports retention while the four misses require a representative comparison before claiming retrieval superiority. Memory recall and code search receipts do not qualify financial answer truth or historical market availability.
limitations: Twelve curated queries are a bounded diagnostic, not an independent holdout or a complete financial RAG evaluation. Exact-source recall at three was 8/12; misses remain recorded.

The eight native answer invocations form four within-provider task comparisons; two Claude full-context answers missed the word protocol and one focused Codex answer scored 9.5 versus 10. These are not general or causal savings results.
Same-host encrypted restore preserved application state, but independent key recovery, off-host durability and new-host client rebinding remain unqualified.
Alternative memory and RAG repositories below were generally source-reviewed, not run head-to-head. A source-only candidate has not failed.

Current primary-source review corrects manual-only, Claude-only and cloud-only exclusions. No matched memory benchmark or new installation was run; automatic capture, local providers and published scores remain source claims until exercised on the selected profile.
domain_rows.overturn_when: Run a preregistered, representative held-out financial/document and code retrieval set at the same context budget; replace or supplement a lane only if a candidate improves source/answer fidelity, abstention and measured task cost while preserving isolation, exact source recovery and native client behavior.

candidates.name: Context Mode

domain_rows.title: Native research workers and operations
domain_rows.requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
domain_rows.current_choice: Native Codex and Claude for bounded research and review; Dagu/systemd for selected local command workflows; one OpenTelemetry Collector with Prometheus/Loki/Grafana; native sandboxing and Restic for their separately qualified scopes. Optional gateways and agent frameworks remain task-specific.
domain_rows.rationale: The retained native lane has actual task results, process/usage observations and local command workflow history. Adding an agent framework or gateway by default would not close a demonstrated requirement and can alter account identity, tool behavior or retry ownership. Dagu's accepted local scope fits existing commands; larger workflow and data platforms become preferable only when their durability, partitioning or operational requirements are real.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
domain_rows.overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.

candidates.name: Codex
candidates.rationale: The native CLI/app-server worker preserves the supported account, tool and session path and has real bounded research results. The official API Agents SDK is a different application integration, not an interchangeable subscription-backed worker.

candidates.name: Claude Code
candidates.rationale: Native independent review and research tasks have returned results and scoped usage observations. Retain this lane while checking actual account readiness and preserving failed or protocol-incomplete attempts.

candidates.name: Dagu
candidates.rationale: The native local scheduler runs existing bounded commands, retains authenticated history and has accepted research packet/Parquet preparation. The historical card's conditional label does not negate those later selected local operations.

candidates.name: OpenTelemetry Collector contrib
candidates.rationale: One accepted distribution supplies privacy transforms and native metric/log delivery. The core Collector repository is a source dependency, not a second collector to install.

candidates.name: Prometheus
candidates.rationale: The accepted metric store supports independently scoped process observations and alert rules. Historical missing initial samples remain limitations rather than retroactively repaired counts.

candidates.name: Loki
candidates.rationale: The existing privacy-filtered log lane complements metrics and has native process correlation evidence. It does not imply retention of full conversation transcripts.

candidates.name: Grafana
candidates.rationale: It reads the existing Prometheus/Loki stores and has retained dashboard evidence. A new trace/evaluation suite is conditional on a question the current observation stack cannot answer.

candidates.name: Restic
candidates.rationale: Native encrypted backup/restore plus original-application restoration now covers scoped ai-memory and Qdrant state. This supports current local recovery while leaving independent keys and off-host durability open.

candidates.name: Temporal
candidates.rationale: Durable activities, waiting and host-loss recovery are a plausible escalation for multi-day effects. The existing bounded command workload has not demonstrated the need or qualified a Temporal deployment.

candidates.name: Prefect
candidates.rationale: A Python-first flow service can fit scheduling/retries if that becomes the main operational requirement. It remains an alternative to adding another retry owner around current native workflows.

candidates.name: Dagster
candidates.rationale: Partitioned assets, lineage and backfills may justify adoption for the data program. Those merits do not establish benefit for simply dispatching a few native research workers.

candidates.name: LangGraph
candidates.rationale: Explicit agent state/checkpoints can help once branching and resume exceed a bounded native task. No matched task establishes that another agent loop is currently needed.

candidates.name: DeerFlow
candidates.rationale: One retained embedded DeerFlow ACP research prompt completed; current source also documents embedded Python, terminal, sandbox and Claude/native-provider integrations. These are substantial prebuilt capabilities, but the full planner/UI service and current revision have not been locally qualified. The tested adapter's read-only label mapped to workspaceWrite/on-request, so preserve that historical restriction finding rather than assuming the outer harness fixes it.

candidates.name: OmniRoute
candidates.rationale: Scoped installation, service and plaintext restore worked, while the September 20 inference attempt hit quota/429 limits and compression previews lost a required value. Keep optional explicit routing with compression disabled; these observations do not prove the gateway universally unusable.

candidates.name: FreeLLMAPI
candidates.rationale: The retained Windows-to-WSL health result proves transport only; Claude-like aliases can select local Qwen and do not establish Anthropic identity or Astra inference. It cannot silently replace the native worker.

candidates.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
candidates.rationale: Appropriate for an application-owned API agent with programmatic control when that is the requirement. It has not demonstrated a missing capability in the selected native Codex research path.

candidates.name: vLLM
candidates.rationale: Retain the accepted 0.25.0 WSL embedding runtime: 0.29.0 installed and its CLI ran, but GPU startup failed with unavailable UVA on this host. This is a concrete version/hardware boundary, not a failure of all newer releases or other hosts.

candidates.name: Deep Agents
candidates.rationale: The reviewed harness combines planning, delegated context, filesystem backends and LangGraph persistence. It is a credible prebuilt application-owned worker alternative, including local model routes; neither its README nor the available upstream tests establish better catalog-review accuracy, native-account compatibility or total cost on our tasks.

candidates.name: OpenHands SDK
candidates.rationale: The maintained SDK/Agent Server owns agents, tools, conversations, events and local or ephemeral workspaces; it is a credible isolated/remote-worker implementation. No matched native research, interruption/recovery or complete operating-cost comparison has displaced the accepted worker path.

candidates.name: OpenHands Agent Canvas
candidates.rationale: The current repository is Agent Canvas, a control center able to host OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex and other ACP agents across backends. Treat it as a prospective host for existing native workers, not merely a competing coding model. Its hosting, account boundaries, persistence and migration remain unqualified here.

candidates.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
candidates.rationale: The primary source provides .NET/Python agent applications, provider integrations and graph workflows with checkpoints and handoffs. It closes a source-review coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime gap; qualify a required application workflow and deployment before adoption.

domain_rows.title: Market data, filings and causal research datasets
domain_rows.requirement: Acquire licensed, source-identifiable US-equity observations; preserve feed, timestamps, identity and corporate actions; produce exact reproducible analytical snapshots and reject data whose historical availability or eligibility is unknown.
domain_rows.current_choice: Official alpaca-py for the bounded selected market-data path; EdgarTools for selected filing parsing/acquisition; DuckDB and Parquet for local analysis; exchange_calendars for explicit session semantics. Dataset manifests and schema checks are requirements, while DVC/Pandera remain source-reviewed implementation candidates.
domain_rows.rationale: Native acquisition, parsing and analytical receipts support these concrete interfaces without a new lake, broker or distributed database. They do not close the actual research bottleneck: a complete point-in-time eligible universe with trustworthy availability, identity and corporate-action semantics. Source-review defaults for DVC/Pandera must not be mistaken for installed acceptance. Databento/Massive are credible conditional alternatives when required coverage or rights cannot be obtained through the selected path.
limitations: The authenticated Alpaca receipt covers 25 AAPL SIP/raw daily bars and two corporate actions over five successful pages, not a survivorship-free universe, complete history or real-time feed entitlement.

Numeric corporate-action values matched the frozen probe, but missing dividend currency prevented full cash-unit reconciliation. Original historical availability and complete action coverage remain open.
Three documentary lifecycle cases preserve observed cutoffs and source anchors; retrospective claims do not establish historical as-known eligibility or permanent security identity.
The prior SEC HTTP 403 remains a historical failure. Later corrected acquisition and parsing qualify their selected requests only; no general filing-completeness or strategy-validity claim follows.
SQL, schemas and content hashes cannot repair missing provenance, revised fundamentals, access rights or outcome-selected samples.
domain_rows.overturn_when: Freeze required universe/history/latency, rights, correction and availability semantics; compare selected providers on representative securities including delistings, ticker reuse and corporate actions, then change the feed/store only when a candidate closes those gaps with auditable records and acceptable measured cost. Add a server or lake only after local throughput/concurrency measurements justify it.

candidates.name: alpaca-py
candidates.rationale: The official SDK matches the chosen broker and provides measured bounded data acquisition plus a separately qualified paper smoke path. Historical source-only card language is superseded only for the exact later receipts, not all endpoints or entitlements.

candidates.name: EdgarTools
candidates.rationale: Selected SEC acquisition and native offline parsing preserve filing/document anchors. Keep the richer parser where that structured output is useful; original availability and historical security eligibility remain separate.

candidates.name: DuckDB

candidates.name: exchange_calendars

candidates.name: Databento
candidates.rationale: A reviewed candidate for licensed exchange-level history/replay and point-in-time reference data when those requirements exceed the selected acquisition path. No paid dataset or matched acquisition comparison was run for this choice.

candidates.name: Massive Python client
candidates.rationale: Consolidated data, reference and news interfaces warrant comparison against the exact required history, correction and permitted-use contract. Catalog inclusion is not subscription entitlement or coverage evidence.

candidates.name: OpenBB
candidates.rationale: A normalized research interface can remove bespoke adapters when several providers are required. It does not create data rights or missing history and currently adds another layer to an accepted direct SDK path.

candidates.name: sec-edgar-downloader
candidates.rationale: A smaller raw-filings collector is reasonable if structured EdgarTools parsing is unnecessary. No current gap warrants operating two overlapping collectors for the same source set.

candidates.name: Polars
candidates.rationale: Expression-based transforms may be clearer or faster for a defined workload. No same-data correctness/performance comparison presently justifies replacing the native SQL/Parquet path.

candidates.name: QuestDB
candidates.rationale: Sustained tick ingestion and concurrent time-series queries could justify a server. Current bounded files do not demonstrate that requirement, and no deployment benchmark is recorded.

candidates.name: ClickHouse
candidates.rationale: Shared large scans and aggregations can justify its operational footprint once measured local limits appear. This is a scale option, not a defeated competitor.

candidates.name: DVC
candidates.rationale: The historical default is a source-reviewed candidate for dataset hashes and dependency manifests. The selected portable runtime has no claimed DVC-native dataset acceptance; simple retained manifests do not imply DVC installation.

candidates.name: Pandera
candidates.rationale: A reviewed compact schema-validation candidate, with real market schemas and fail-closed promotion still requiring implementation. Schema acceptance cannot establish provider completeness or prevent every form of leakage.

candidates.name: lakeFS
candidates.rationale: Atomic object-store branches and promotion gates may serve concurrent teams. The present local snapshots have not established a need for that additional service.

candidates.name: yfinance
candidates.rationale: Convenient exploratory access does not satisfy the authoritative automated-trading data contract's rights and historical-quality requirements. The disposition is a requirement boundary, not a measured assertion that every returned price is wrong.

candidates.name: pandas exact timestamp support
candidates.rationale: Existing supporting dependency accepted for strict exact nanosecond timestamp parsing. Retain its tested contract alongside DuckDB/Parquet; this is not a general dataframe-performance win over Polars or Arrow.

domain_rows.title: Simulation, broker adapters and strategy qualification
domain_rows.requirement: Use the selected NautilusTrader destination with broker-specific execution boundaries, deterministic numeric risk and reproducible equity accounting; preserve the prior LEAN oracle and qualify any strategy with causal data, costs and independent reconciliation.
domain_rows.current_choice: NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 is the user-selected destination; LEAN remains the retained historical comparison engine. Nautilus native IBKR awaits broker acceptance; Alpaca uses official alpaca-py and a separately qualified deterministic paper path. No strategy is promoted as profitable.
domain_rows.rationale: The current choice follows the explicit runtime target and supported native IBKR direction, with real installation/replay and bounded AAPL accounting evidence. LEAN has deeper retained SPY stress/dividend/cash evidence and is kept as the comparison oracle rather than relabeled a losing engine. The AAPL diagnostic and one Alpaca paper roundtrip do not prove SPY parity, realistic liquidity, IBKR operation, continuous paper service or a winning strategy. Existing research modules remain task-specific.
limitations: Nautilus 2.0.0rc5 is a prerelease. The old September 19 Nautilus alternative and LEAN default cards remain historical; runtime-target.json governs the current destination.

The retained AAPL replay has 15 bars and five roundtrips per baseline/stress scenario with reconciled cash; it excludes known action dates and uses retrospective synthetic close fills with unlimited modeled depth.
SPY/LEAN dividend/cash parity is still planned. LEAN's known-crash fixtures are engineering stresses, not untouched holdout results or calibrated broker execution.

The Alpaca trial observed two actual writes, a -0.08 USD cash-matched gross result, flat/idle reconciliation and completed-trial recovery with zero additional writes. In-flight native failure cases, IBKR, live operation and continuous paper operation remain open.
No accepted point-in-time universe, extreme-mover/catalyst strategy, financing-inclusive performance or deployable profitability follows from these receipts.

Independent source review found two bare matches! expressions that do not assert denial-event variants in Nautilus risk tests, also present in v2.0.0rc5 source. Other tests assert denial and reasons. This narrow test defect is not an observed runtime failure; see docs/blind-catalog-source-adjudication-20260921.md.
domain_rows.overturn_when: Reopen the implementation choice if Nautilus cannot preserve a required cash/order semantic, fails a preregistered SPY/LEAN parity tolerance, or a broker-specific adapter cannot pass ownership, reconciliation, partial/cancel/reconnect and numeric risk cases. Compare alternatives on the same frozen inputs and failure contract; promote a strategy only after independent temporal and cost-aware evaluation.
